extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant reviewers and applicants (K01 career development applicants) assessing the Facilities & Other Resources section
extracted.subtask_description: A Facilities & Other Resources section from an NIH K01 career development grant describing institutional infrastructure, core facilities, personnel, equipment, and institutional support to justify feasibility and environment for the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall institutional research infrastructure and environment
rubrics_metrics.description: The research infrastructure at Cincinnati Children’s Hospital Medical Center (CCHMC) and at the University of Michigan including facilities, personnel, faculty, students, and equipment is among the best in the nation and provides the ideal environment for carrying out the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative emphasizes institutional scale (large research space, historic endowment, NIH funding levels), breadth of research divisions, publication record, and a statement that the environment contributes to the success of the proposed research and career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative and regulatory support
rubrics_metrics.description: Research administration and regulatory oversight groups oversee a total research budget and the Office for Research Compliance and Regulatory Affairs (ORCRA) and the Office of Sponsored Programs offer educational opportunities including sessions addressing informed consent, writing clinical study protocols, grant budgetary management, and IRB issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect institutional offices to provide training, assistance with protocol/consent/IRB, budget management, and post-award support. Presence of these offices supports efficient conduct and compliance of studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects protection accreditation (AAHRPP)
rubrics_metrics.description: CCHMC received accreditation from the Association for the Accreditation of Human Research Protection Programs (AAHRPP) in 2007.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AAHRPP accreditation signals robust human subjects protections and is presented as evidence of institutional compliance infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedicated IRB liaison / research compliance specialist
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division has a dedicated institutional review board liaison ('research compliance specialist') who assists with efficiently developing and modifying protocols to facilitate research while maintaining strict protection of human subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A named liaison facilitates protocol development/changes and speeds regulatory processing while ensuring compliance — an explicit resource reviewers expect for human subjects work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of clinical research personnel/support
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to a Clinical Research Manager, Clinical Research Coordinators (CRCs), a Regulatory Coordinator, and a Grants Specialist; division-level CRCs will aid in sample collection and enrollment and maintain documentation in compliance with HIPAA and human subjects’ regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailing specific staff roles and number of coordinators supports feasibility claims (who will enroll, collect samples, manage documentation and regulatory files).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical patient volume and population adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: High patient volumes cited (Division cares for >25,000 encounters/year; ED had over 92,000 visits in 2014; Emergency Department sees >1100 cases of community-acquired pneumonia annually) to demonstrate access to study populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantified patient volumes are used to justify recruitment feasibility for the proposed clinical research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division-level research infrastructure in Emergency Medicine
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division of Emergency Medicine has a sophisticated infrastructure including a Research Team (Clinical Research Manager, Supervisors, Financial Analyst, ten CRCs, Regulatory Coordinator, Quality Assurance Specialist, Grants Specialist) to assist investigators with all aspects of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The enumerated team roles indicate availability of study design support, enrollment, QA, regulatory oversight, and budget management at the divisional level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to multi-institutional research networks (PECARN)
rubrics_metrics.description: Membership/leadership in the Pediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network (PECARN), a federally funded pediatric emergency medicine research network of 18 pediatric EDs, providing a home for multi-center pneumonia projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access to established research networks enables multicenter studies, larger sample sizes, and collaborative opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biostatistics and epidemiology expertise and Data Management Center (DMC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division of Biostatistics and Epidemiology (DBE) offers broad expertise, numerous faculty/staff, and a Data Management Center that supported 90 studies in 2015 with database development, data entry, discrepancy management, data cleaning and preparation for analysis; DBE maintains REDCap and performs quality checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability of statistical consultation, a DMC, REDCap, and routine quality checks are presented as essential resources for rigorous study design and data integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biomedical informatics support and EMR data extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division of Biomedical Informatics (BMI) supports researchers with data storage systems, database servers, collaboration tools, and extracts and maintains clinical data from electronic medical records into secure REDCap databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BMI capability to extract EMR data to REDCap is highlighted as a resource for efficient, secure clinical data capture and integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computing resources, software, and secure servers
rubrics_metrics.description: PI and staff have desktop/laptop computers with standard word processing, bibliographic and data management software; SAS version 9.3.2 and a server-based SAS on HP ProLiant DL585 with 32 GB RAM and dedicated storage (initial 500 GB per user); server is in secure data center and backed up daily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit mention of analysis software (SAS), server specs, secure backups, and available disk space supports computational feasibility for data analysis and storage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical office space and administrative support
rubrics_metrics.description: Division office space (10,200 sq ft) includes private offices, conference rooms, huddle offices, workstations, and PI has a lockable office with multiple locking file cabinets and access to an administrative assistant and CRCs in the same suite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protected office space, proximity to mentors, and on-site administrative help are cited to support productive research workflow and data security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical laboratory accreditation and SOPs (CLIA, CAP)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Clinical Laboratory at CCHMC is CLIA-certified and College of American Pathologists-accredited with standard operating procedures in place to ensure reliable and reproducible test results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accredited clinical labs with SOPs are necessary for dependable biomarker/clinical testing used in translational studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory for Specialized Clinical Studies (LSCS) capabilities and GLP compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: LSCS (20-year history) is CAP- and CLIA-accredited; all assays are conducted following GLP guidelines; extensive documentation is maintained; laboratory QA officer and independent regulatory affairs department support services; approved for Biosafety Level 2 (BL2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GLP adherence, QA oversight, and regulatory support indicate assay validity, auditability, and compliance for research assays (e.g., quantitative PCR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized assay capability (PCR, quantitative PCR, viral and bacterial assays)
rubrics_metrics.description: LSCS will perform quantitative real-time PCR (to measure pneumococcal bacterial load), respiratory viral PCR and M. pneumoniae PCR; Clinical Laboratories perform conventional biomarker testing including CBC, C-reactive protein and blood cultures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of validated molecular and conventional assays required by the project demonstrates technical feasibility for primary endpoints and sample analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory biosafety and sample handling practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Labs operate under Biosafety Level 2 regulations, follow NIH microbiological practices, have trained personnel for blood/urine/nasopharyngeal samples, limit access during work, require PPE and follow Standard Precautions and institutional infection control policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit biosafety and sample handling protocols ensure safe, compliant processing of human specimens and reduce contamination/exposure risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biorepository capacity, storage redundancy and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Cincinnati Biobank Core Facility (CBCF) provides specimen storage (on-site and off-site facilities), multiple freezer units (-80°C, -20°C), walk-in freezer, liquid nitrogen storage, monitored alarm systems and emergency generators; each freezer operates on a unique circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redundant storage locations, alarmed freezers and generator backup are presented as measures to protect specimen integrity and continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biobank personnel and laboratory automation/equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: CBCF has ten full-time employees including PhD-level director and database manager; equipment includes AutoGenFlex STAR automated DNA extraction, Promega Maxwell 16, Fluidigm EP1 HX microfluidics, Trinean DropSense 96 spectrophotometer, centrifuges and other standard lab equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staffing and automated instrumentation support high-throughput, standardized specimen processing and high-quality extraction/measurement workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen tracking and inventory management software
rubrics_metrics.description: The CBCF uses specimen tracking software, Biomaterial Tracking and Management, to electronically record the location and availability of every aliquot of every specimen collected from each patient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic specimen tracking enables traceability, auditability, and efficient retrieval of aliquots for analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: NMR-based metabolomics core instrumentation and analytical workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: The NBMC provides 1H NMR metabolomics with a Bruker IVDr 600MHz NMR system (fully-automated, SampleJet autosampler) and access to a Varian 800MHz NMR at UC COM; analysis uses TopSpin, AMIX and Chenomx software with automated methodologies (ANOVA, PCA, PLS), binning of spectra (0.01-0.005ppm), generation of 1H SDS and FDR control at the 0.05 level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes instrumentation, software, and statistical approaches (including FDR control) to identify significantly different NMR peaks between study groups; indicates capacity for both broad and targeted metabolomics.

rubrics_metrics.name: NMR core sample storage and safety practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Samples not immediately analyzed are stored in an -80°C freezer in locked core lab space; staff use PPE; residual specimens disposed in biohazard containers; samples transported in biohazard bags to minimize exposure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specimen storage, transport, and disposal procedures conform to biosafety practices and preserve sample integrity for metabolomics.

rubrics_metrics.name: LC/MS and mass spectrometry instrumentation and capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Ziady LC/MS2 lab and the (MRC)2 core provide a suite of instruments including Agilent GC/MS systems, Agilent Triple Quadrupole 6410/6490 with Agilent 1290 UHPLC, Agilent LC/MSD Time-of-flight, Quadrupole TOF instruments, and Jasco HPLC systems; capability for both directed (MRM) and untargeted metabolomics, ESI and APCI ionization modes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed instrument list and modes indicate capacity for high-sensitivity targeted assays and broad untargeted profiling, structural elucidation (MS/MS), and high throughput analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory information management system (LIMS) and data archiving
rubrics_metrics.description: (MRC)2 uses LIMS to barcode samples, schedule chromatographic runs, track raw data files by LIMS identifiers, provide a web-based secure interface, and archive data files (e.g., to DVD at intervals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LIMS-based sample and data tracking ensures reproducible workflows, traceability, and secure access for data processing and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assay precision and quality metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Directed assays at (MRC)2 typically result in coefficients of variation (COV) values of 15%-20% for analytes such as amino acids, acyl-carnitines, glycolytic and TCA intermediates, steroids, and other biochemical compound classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing expected assay precision (COV) gives reviewers an empirical measure of assay reproducibility and analytical quality for planned measurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlled reagent procurement and batch consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: For metabolomics assays conducted in (MRC)2, all solvents are purchased in bulk from a single manufacturer’s lot in sufficient quantity to complete planned experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using single-lot reagents reduces batch effects and supports data comparability across runs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical and bioinformatics support for complex datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: (MRC)2 and affiliated faculty provide a network of statisticians and bioinformatics faculty/staff to help interpret large untargeted datasets and method development for metabolomics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access to statistical and bioinformatics expertise is highlighted as necessary for correct interpretation of high-dimensional metabolomics data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center for Clinical and Translational Research (CCTST) services
rubrics_metrics.description: CCTST coordinates services including biostatistics, biomedical informatics, data management, training grant application assistance, inpatient/outpatient clinical research services, community engagement support, regulatory knowledge, and institutional programs such as KL2/K12 and pilot grant programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central translational cores and training programs provide methodological, operational, and career development resources that contribute to project success and trainee advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty development, mentorship and peer-support structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Office for Faculty Development sponsors seminars (recorded/archived) on collaborations, goal setting, scientific writing, negotiation; the 'K club' provides peer mentorship for those applying for or holding NIH career development awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentorship programs, seminars and peer groups are presented as institutional supports that increase the likelihood of career development award success and transition to independent funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library and literature resources with librarian support
rubrics_metrics.description: CCHMC Pratt Library and University of Cincinnati Health Sciences Library provide access to hundreds to thousands of print and electronic journal subscriptions and employ full-time librarians to assist with literature searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ready access to literature and librarian assistance supports rigorous background research, systematic reviews, and manuscript preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional commitment to early investigator support and career transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional support for early investigators through internal grants, administrative support, structured opportunities for networking and education, and programs aimed at ensuring successful completion of K awards and transition to R01 funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit institutional commitment and internal mechanisms for career development strengthen the case that the K award will enable progression to independent research funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: External collaborator facilities and access (University of Michigan cores)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaboration with University of Michigan resources including Stringer Laboratory (sample processing, lyophilizers, -20/-80 freezers), CoP Biochemical NMR Core (Varian 500 NMR, VNMRJ software), and the (MRC)2 regional metabolomics core with extensive mass spec resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-institutional access to additional specialized equipment and expertise (NMR, LC/MS) is cited to augment home-institution capabilities and ensure completion of proposed assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical security and data/specimen backup systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Server backups are performed nightly; freezers are alarm-monitored with emergency generators; server located in secure data center; freezers operate on unique circuits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailing backup, monitoring and power-redundancy measures demonstrates planning to protect data and specimens from loss or equipment failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlled access to specialized equipment and training requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to imaging and analysis suites is controlled by keycard and user login; some core access (e.g., Ziady imaging suite) will require PI training during the award period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access controls and training plans ensure appropriate use of specialized equipment and that investigators will acquire necessary technical competence during the award.
